blocks.heading: Ma-Fork: Your Postgraduate Track Decides the Door

items.text: Feeds directly into Archives and government record roles
Write one short archival note, one museum object label, one explainer article, or one mock lesson.
A short, honest conversation with a curator, archivist, NET-qualified teacher, or content researcher beats hours of reading generic career blogs about the role.
Archives, museums, archaeology, publishing, and heritage tourism are real, functioning career tracks with their own hiring bodies and pay ladders.

Private-sector recruiters do not automatically read "history graduate" as a usable skill signal the way they read "commerce graduate with Excel" or "engineering graduate with a GitHub profile." A multiplier skill has to sit visibly on top of the degree.

blocks.heading: Fresh Reporter and Editorial Roles Typically Start

figures.label: Entry Level Pay
figures.source: Fresh reporter and editorial roles typically start around Rs 2.5-5 LPA. History graduates have a genuine edge in long-form explainer content, historical nonfiction editing, and documentary or streaming-platform research, roles that reward exactly the source-checking and synthesis skill a history degree builds.

blocks.heading: Museums and Heritage Management

figures.label: Typical Salary Range
figures.source: Entry-level assistant curator roles typically pay roughly Rs 30,000-45,000 a month, mid-level curator or gallery-manager roles Rs 60,000-90,000, and senior director-level roles Rs 1.5-3 lakh a month or more. INTACH, state museums, and private heritage trusts are the main hiring bodies alongside government museums.

blocks.heading: Teaching and Research: NET, JRF, and ICHR

figures.label: Typical Salary Range
figures.source: UGC NET JRF pays roughly Rs 37,000 a month for the first two years, rising to about Rs 42,000 as a Senior Research Fellow. ICHR's own Junior Research Fellowship for history PhD scholars pays less, around Rs 17,600 a month plus a small annual contingency grant, awarded through its own entrance exam and interview. Government college assistant professor basic pay starts near Rs 57,700 (roughly Rs 90,000-1.1 lakh gross with allowances); private colleges commonly pay Rs 40,000-60,000 for the same designation.
